learn.title: Rooftop Solar and Net Metering in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar transforms urban spaces into clean energy generators, helping India meet its 2030 renewable targets. Net metering enables households to sell excess power back to the grid, creating financial incentives and reducing carbon footprints across Indian cities and towns.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using photovoltaic cells. A typical 1 kW rooftop system generates 4-5 kWh daily in India. The DC electricity is inverted to AC for home use, with any surplus fed back to the local grid through a bidirectional meter.
learn.c2_text: Net metering credits surplus power fed into the grid against electricity consumed. Under Indian standards, consumers pay only for the net difference. For every unit exported, one unit is credited. This policy applies up to 100% of contracted load, encouraging widespread adoption.
learn.c3_text: MNRE's net metering rules apply to consumers with 1-100 kW capacity. States like Gujarat and Karnataka lead in rooftop installations. As of 2024, India has 9.5 GW of rooftop solar capacity, with targets of 40 GW by 2022 now being pursued aggressively.

learn.stat2: Average 1 kW system produces 4-5 kWh daily in Indian conditions
learn.stat3: Net metering allows 1:1 credit for exported units
learn.stat4: Policy applies up to 100% of contracted load capacity

learn.title: Wind Resource Assessment for Developers
learn.intro: Finding optimal wind sites requires sophisticated resource assessment to maximize energy yield and project viability. IRENA's guidelines help developers identify high-quality wind resources, ensuring cost-effective projects that contribute significantly to global clean energy transitions and carbon reduction goals.
learn.c1_text: Developers deploy anemometers at 10-120m heights for 12+ months to measure wind speed and direction. The data captures temporal variability and seasonal patterns. Weibull distribution models predict annual energy production. Accurate measurement is crucial as 10% error in wind speed means 30% error in energy output.
learn.c2_text: Satellite data, numerical weather prediction models, and reanalysis datasets like ERA5 provide large-scale wind assessments. GIS tools combine terrain, land use, and accessibility data to rank sites. Developers also use mesoscale atmospheric models for micro-siting decisions within wind farms.
learn.c3_text: India's wind resources are concentrated in Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, and Rajasthan. The Indian Wind Power Association uses similar IRENA methodologies for site evaluation. Post-2024, India aims for 60 GW wind capacity, requiring rigorous resource assessment to ensure grid-compatible projects and optimal land use.

learn.stat2: 10% wind speed error causes 30% energy output error
learn.stat3: Tamil Nadu leads Indian wind installations with 9 GW

learn.title: Lithium-Ion Battery Storage Explained
learn.intro: Lithium-ion batteries are revolutionizing grid stability and renewable integration through efficient energy storage. The US Department of Energy highlights their role in enabling 24/7 renewable power, providing backup resilience, and supporting electric vehicles - making them essential for a reliable clean energy future.
learn.c1_text: Lithium-ion cells use lithium ions moving between anode and cathode during charge/discharge cycles. A typical 100 kWh residential battery stores enough energy for 2-3 days of household use. Energy density ranges 250-300 Wh/kg, with round-trip efficiency of 85-95% for grid applications.
learn.c2_text: Batteries provide frequency regulation by absorbing excess generation or discharging during peaks. They enable renewable firming through 4-hour to 12-hour storage. Peak shaving reduces grid stress, while black start capabilities restore power after outages. Microgrids use batteries for islanding and resilience.
learn.c3_text: India's 2030 target includes 500 GWh of energy storage. Major utilities deploy battery systems for solar smoothing. The Saubhagya scheme uses batteries for rural microgrids. Steel plants in Tamil Nadu use 10 MWh battery systems for peak shaving, demonstrating commercial viability in Indian industrial sectors.
learn.stat1: US grid-scale storage reached 12.6 GW in 2023

learn.title: Power Purchase Agreements Explained
learn.intro: Power Purchase Agreements unlock renewable energy financing by connecting developers with corporate buyers. IRENA explains how these long-term contracts de-risk investments, enabling massive renewable deployment while providing predictable returns for project developers and stable energy costs for corporations transitioning to clean energy.
learn.c1_text: A PPA is a long-term contract where a buyer purchases electricity at a fixed rate for 10-25 years. The developer builds and operates the plant, transferring all construction and operational risks. Corporate PPAs include virtual options allowing financial hedging without physical delivery, popular with tech companies seeking RECs.
learn.c2_text: Banks finance projects based on PPA-backed cash flows, reducing investor risk. Debt service coverage ratios of 1.2-1.5 ensure repayment capacity. The contracted price typically covers levelized cost of electricity plus modest return. This structure enabled 20 GW of renewable capacity globally through 2023.
learn.c3_text: Indian corporations like Tata Power and Reliance signed 5 GW of renewable PPAs by 2024. The Green Energy Corral initiative facilitates corporate procurement. Steel and IT sectors lead adoption, with average tariffs dropping 25% since 2020. Karnataka and Gujarat dominate corporate renewable procurement.
learn.stat1: Global renewable PPAs reached 20 GW in 2023
learn.stat2: Corporate PPAs reduce electricity costs by 15-30%
learn.stat3: India corporate renewable procurement at 5 GW

learn.title: HVDC Transmission Lines Explained
learn.intro: High Voltage Direct Current transmission enables efficient power delivery across vast distances with minimal losses. The IEA emphasizes HVDC's critical role in connecting renewable-rich regions to load centers, building resilient grids that support global clean energy transitions and energy security objectives worldwide.
learn.c1_text: HVDC transmits power with lower losses over 500+ km compared to AC lines. Losses are 3-5% per 1000 km versus 10-15% for HVAC. Converter stations transform AC to DC and back, using thyristors or IGBTs. The technology enables asynchronous grid connections between different frequency systems.
learn.c2_text: HVDC connects offshore wind farms and remote hydro plants to population centers. It enables supercontinental grids like the proposed Asia Super Grid. Benefits include 30% lower transmission costs for long distances, improved power quality, and enhanced grid stability through fast control responses (milliseconds).
learn.c3_text: India's ±800 kV Ultra High Voltage DC link from Chhattisgarh to Delhi spans 1400 km, transmitting 6 GW. The Green Energy Corridor project plans 5 GW HVDC capacity by 2030. These lines connect renewable-rich central India to industrial corridors, enabling integration of 500 GW renewable target while maintaining grid stability.

learn.title: Perovskite Solar Cells Next Gen
learn.intro: Perovskite solar cells promise unprecedented efficiency gains beyond silicon limitations, potentially doubling photovoltaic technology performance. NREL highlights how these materials could reduce manufacturing costs, enable flexible applications, and accelerate the global transition to affordable, high-performance renewable energy through breakthrough semiconductor science.
learn.c1_text: Perovskites have calcium titanate crystal structure ABX3, where lead iodide forms the light-absorbing layer. They solution-process at low temperatures, enabling roll-to-roll manufacturing. Single-junction cells achieved 25.7% efficiency in lab tests. Tandem perovskite-silicon devices have reached 33.7% efficiency, surpassing silicon's 26.8% record.
learn.c2_text: Perovskite production uses printing techniques, cutting costs 50-70% versus silicon's high-temperature processes. They're lightweight and flexible, enabling building-integrated PV and portable applications. Stability challenges remain, but encapsulation and compositional engineering now achieve 25-year lifespans. Pilot lines are emerging in China and Europe.
learn.c3_text: NREL's chart shows perovskite-silicon tandems leading efficiency rankings. Oxford PV began commercial production in 2024, targeting 30% efficiency modules. The US Department of Energy's Solar Energy Technologies Office funds 100+ perovskite projects. India's CSIR and IIMs are establishing perovskite research centers for tropical climate adaptation.
learn.stat3: Oxford PV began commercial production in 2024
